Football.title: Mohamed Salah could make Liverpool return at Manchester City in FA Cup
Football.content:
Liverpool are hopeful that Mohamed Salah will return from injury in the FA Cup quarter-final against Manchester City on Saturday as the Egypt international prepares for his emotional farewell tour.

Salah missed Liverpool’s defeat at Brighton before the international break with a muscle problem sustained in the Champions League rout of Galatasaray. The 33-year-old forward, who announced last week that he would be leaving Liverpool at the end of the season, was also forced to miss Egypt’s friendlies against Saudi Arabia and Spain. The Pharaohs face the latter in Barcelona on Tuesday.

The forward has responded well to treatment and there is confidence he will be involved at the Etihad Stadium, when Arne Slot’s side embark on a sequence of fixtures that could define their season.

Alexander Isak may also be available for the first time since fracturing a leg at Tottenham in December, although the Champions League quarter-final first leg at Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday week is considered a more realistic date for his comeback. The £125m British-record signing is expected to resume team training this week.

There is less encouraging fitness news on Alisson, however, with Liverpool’s first-choice goalkeeper still nursing a hamstring injury sustained on the eve of the Brighton game. Alisson, 33, has experienced repeated hamstring injuries in recent seasons and remains a major doubt for the trip to Parc des Princes, where he performed heroics last season to help Liverpool to win their Champions League last-16 first leg.

Florian Wirtz, meanwhile, has claimed he has become a stronger player as a result of the problems he encountered after moving to Liverpool. The Germany international joined for a then club-record £116m from Bayer Leverkusen last summer but has struggled to impose himself in the Premier League, producing four goals and two assists. Speaking to the German television programme Sportschau, the 22-year-old insisted he was adapting to the physical nature of English football after a difficult start.

“It wasn’t an easy phase,” Wirtz said on his first few months at Liverpool. “It’s sometimes good that things don’t always go upwards and that you experience a dip and grow stronger because of it. That’s how I see it now as well – it has made me a bit stronger. I had to overcome resistance and adapt. I had to learn to become stronger and hold on to the ball.”

Football.title: Interpol arrest warrant requested in Congo-Brazzaville for Jean-Guy Blaise Mayolas
Football.content:
Authorities in Congo-Brazzaville have applied to Interpol for an international arrest warrant against Jean-Guy Blaise Mayolas, the president of the country’s football federation, Fecofoot, after he was convicted of embezzling $1.1m in Fifa funds.

Mayolas is on the run with his wife and son after they were all sentenced to life imprisonment this month for embezzling funds provided by world football’s governing body as part of its Covid-19 relief plan in February 2021. As the Guardian revealed last year, that included almost $500,000 earmarked for the Congo women’s team.

Mayolas and his family were tried in absentia and are believed to have fled the country weeks before the hearing. Investigators suspect he may be hiding in Cameroon or the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The authorities and partner police forces in the region have been alerted and officials are working with financial intelligence units, including Tracfin, the French financial intelligence unit, to freeze assets linked to the case.

Mayolas and his family members were convicted of money laundering, forgery, use of forged documents and embezzlement on 10 March by the court in Brazzaville, along with Fecofoot’s general secretary, Badji Mombo Wantete, and treasurer, Raoul Kanda. Wantete and Kanda were each sentenced to five years in prison.

Fifa opened disciplinary proceedings against Mayolas, Wantete and Kanda last week for alleged financial misconduct. The charges under consideration include conflict of interest, forgery and improper acceptance of gifts after Fifa’s ethics committee received information and documents during a review.

It has been alleged Mayolas, since being elected as president of Fecofoot in 2018, used a series of shell companies to embezzle funding from Fifa. According to a declaration signed by the presidents of every women’s club in the country’s top flight that was sent to the Congolese authorities in March, $20,000 of the $500,000 Fifa sent to Fecofoot in 2021 as part of its Covid-19 relief plan was paid out.

Mayolas denied all the allegations before his disappearance, describing them as a conspiracy. Wantete also rejected the accusations. In 2015, they received six-month bans from Fifa for ethics violations related to gifts and benefits.

Mayolas was suspended by the country’s sports ministry last year after being investigated for fraud. Fifa stepped in and banned Congo from international football for “third-party interference”, meaning that in March they had to forfeit World Cup qualifiers against Tanzania and Zambia, who were awarded 3-0 victories.

Congo were reinstated when Fecofoot was permitted to resume control of its headquarters in Brazzaville, although Mayolas and Wantete were prevented from travelling to Fifa’s congress in Paraguay and arrested a few days later.

Football.title: Amnesty International warns Fifa World Cup risks becoming ‘stage for repression’
Football.content:
Amnesty International has warned that the World Cup, spread across three North American countries, risks becoming a “stage for repression”. The human rights organisation published a report on Monday – “Humanity Must Win” – calling on Fifa and the host countries, the US, Canada and Mexico, to take urgent action to protect fans, players and other communities.

Fifa has promised a tournament where everyone “feels safe, included and free to exercise their rights”. But Amnesty said that pledge sat in “stark contrast” to conditions in all three host nations, especially the US, which hosts three-quarters of the 104 matches.

Amnesty described the US as facing a “human rights emergency” under the Donald Trump administration, marked by mass deportations, arbitrary arrests and what it called “paramilitary-style” Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) operations. The acting director of ICE said last month the agency would be “a key part of the overall security apparatus for the World Cup”. This comes despite anger at the killing of two American citizens by ICE agents in Minneapolis in January.

Amnesty said none of the published US host city plans addressed how fans or local communities would be protected from ICE operations. Fans from four countries – Côte d’Ivoire, Haiti, Iran and Senegal – face US travel bans and LGBTQ+ fan groups from England and across Europe have said they will not attend matches in the US, citing risks to transgender supporters in particular.

“This World Cup is very far from the ‘medium risk’ tournament Fifa once judged it to be and urgent efforts are needed to bridge the growing gap between the tournament’s original promise and today’s reality,” the report said.

Fifa said this month the 48-team tournament – the biggest World Cup in history – would proceed as scheduled with all teams taking part, despite uncertainty over Iran’s presence due to the conflict in the Middle East.

The global football governing body, heavily criticised over its decision to award a newly created peace prize to president Trump in December, stands to earn $11bn (£8.3bn) from the tournament cycle.

“While Fifa generates record revenues from the 2026 World Cup, fans, communities, players, journalists and workers cannot be made to pay the price,” said Steve Cockburn, Amnesty’s head of economic and social justice. “It is these people – not governments, sponsors or Fifa – to whom football belongs and their rights must be at the centre of the tournament.”

Football.title: WSL talking points: goals galore as Arsenal, Manchester City and Liverpool find derby delight
Football.content:
1 Arsenal firing on all cylinders

With her hat-trick in Arsenal’s 5-2 win over Tottenham, Alessia Russo took her tally to 25 goal contributions in 31 games this campaign. It is a notable return from a player in her prime, not just in her buildup play, but also her finishing. Arsenal’s attacking dominance – they have scored 18 goals in their past five games – is down to the fact that many of their attacking players are in form. Stina Blackstenius has three goals in her past four games while Caitlin Foord also scored on Saturday, her first appearance since returning from the Asian Cup. Renée Slegers has spoken about the versatility in the type of goals her side produces and the need to be ruthless in both penalty areas. Spurs’ two goals meant an end to Arsenal’s 106-day streak of not conceding in the WSL. While all runs must come to an end, Arsenal still boast the meanest defence in the league. Sophie Downey

Match report: Arsenal 5-2 Tottenham

2 Skinner puts loss down to tiredness

Marc Skinner repeatedly said fatigue was Manchester United’s downfall after they were comfortably beaten by Manchester City and expressed his frustration at playing their neighbours on Saturdays straight after midweek Champions League fixtures. His team faced Bayern Munich last Wednesday, whereas City are not in Europe. Asked about the quick turnaround time for this defeat and for November’s 3-0 loss at the Etihad, which also followed a Champions League game for United, Skinner said: “It’s a hard one for me because if I say ‘yes’, which is what I really do feel, then people say it’s an excuse, but it is a factor. I think Man City have had an advantage from that twice this year. That’s [all] the energy they have got; the girls are giving everything. It’s a factor, going into these huge games.” Tom Garry

Match report: Manchester United 0-3 Manchester City

View image in fullscreen Manchester United’s Jess Park and Marc Skinner look dejected at half-time after Vivianne Miedema’s first-half double. Photograph: Molly Darlington/WSL Football/Getty Images

3 Liverpool banish derby woes

Liverpool exemplified their recent improvements by ending their six-year wait for a league victory in a Merseyside derby and a winless run of away WSL fixtures this season with 3-2 win at Goodison Park. Having been winless against Everton in WSL fixtures since May 2019, and having recorded one away WSL win against their neighbours in nearly 13 years, they survived a late Everton rally with 10 players to collect their first away win since Gareth Taylor took over. It lifted them eight points clear of danger at the bottom and they are now surely all but safe, after their successful transfer window. TG

4 Will Siren’s first Hammers goal prove crucial in survival fight?

One instant of brilliance, one swing of the boot that may yet define West Ham’s season. Oona Siren’s first goal for the club, a thunderous volley that left the London City Lionesses goalkeeper, Elene Lete, with no chance, earned a point that could be significant with the Hammers four points clear of Leicester at the bottom with a game in hand. West Ham started brightly, but were punished when Jana Fernández converted the Lionesses’ only shot on target. The response after the break was more purposeful. When Saki Kumagai’s clearance fell invitingly, Siren reacted quickly to drive past Lete. “Every point is important,” she said. With three games remaining this could prove decisive. Mitul Samji

5 Chelsea go second but lack control against Villa

In arguably the most entertaining match of the season, Chelsea’s 4-3 win over Aston Villa was a compelling reminder of their attacking firepower and defensive vulnerability before their Champions League tie against Arsenal on Wednesday. After conceding within two minutes, an end-to-end, almost tennis-like first half ended with six goals scored, Villa converting all three of their shots on target. The Chelsea manager, Sonia Bompastor, expressed her frustration at the loss of control after going 3-1 up, but remained confident her side would respond in the second half. With the Kingsmeadow crowd driving them on, Sam Kerr’s late assist for Sjoeke Nüsken secured a vital victory that moves Chelsea back into second place in the table. Bompastor admitted the winning goal was “a relief for everyone”, but a greater level of control will be required against Arsenal in order to overturn the 3-1 first-leg deficit. Réshma Rao

View image in fullscreen Chelsea lacked control, but Sjoeke Nüsken’s late winner against Aston Villa moved them into second. Photograph: John Walton/PA

6 Brighton happy to have Seike back

Kiko Seike picked up straight where she left off with Brighton and scored for the fourth game in a row for her club to give them a 1-0 win at struggling Leicester. The Japan forward, who scored four goals for her country to help them win the Asia Cup in Australia, is Brighton’s top scorer this term with seven league goals. Her latest owed much to the vision of Fran Kirby, whose defence-splitting pass found Rosa Kafaji who, in turn, set up Seike for the winner, but Seike’s all-round forward play showed she is full of confidence in such a prolific goalscoring run. TG

Football.title: Japan head to Wembley ready to show they’re the real deal before World Cup | John Duerden
Football.content:
Just before the 2002 World Cup, South Korea played Scotland and England in the space of a few days. A 4-1 win against the former in the second city of Busan was followed by a 1-1 draw on the honeymoon island of Jeju, with the future Manchester United teammates Michael Owen and Park Ji-sung the scorers. These results gave the Taegeuk Warriors the confidence to reach the semi finals.

Japan are not on home soil but have lined up the same opposition, beating Scotland 1-0 in Glasgow on Saturday before heading to Wembley on Tuesday.

The hope is that these games will help set the scene for a similarly sensational Japanese summer, especially given this Samurai Blue side are much further along the developmental journey than their east Asian neighbours were 24 years ago and the victory at Hampden Park was a comfortable one for what was a fairly experimental team.

Now it is time for England. Thomas Tuchel would have seen from Saturday’s game that Japan are comfortable on the ball and, after a slow start – understandable given the unfamiliar personnel – the four-time Asian champions can operate with cohesion, clarity and control without really getting out of second gear. In the end it was a deserved win against Scotland, thanks to Junya Ito’s goal, the Genk winger finishing off a fine move late on.

“In the second half we opened up quite a bit and created many chances, which was good because we won,” said Brighton’s Kaoru Mitoma, who came on at the break and impressed. “But it would have been better if we had made it 2-0 or 3-0.”

After four last-16 exits in the past six World Cups, the message coming out of Tokyo is one of ambition; namely reaching the last eight of this summer’s tournament. Fresh from scoring 54 goals in qualification and conceding only three, there is no mystery as to why the team are seeking tougher tests as they prepare for group games against the Netherlands, Tunisia and the winner of Tuesday’s Sweden v Poland playoff. Quite simply, being the best team in Asia is no longer enough. “I want to see how well what we have done until now will work again against a European team,” Mitoma added. “Even if the players change, it is important to see how much of what we have done until now we can still do.”

View image in fullscreen Japan lost to Croatia in the last 16 of the 2022 World Cup, but believe that the quarter-finals – and even beyond – are a realistic target this year. Photograph: Richard Heathcote/Getty Images

When Japan became the first team to qualify for the World Cup last March, the captain, Wataru Endo, told fans at Saitama Stadium that the time when success was getting out of the group was gone. Such sentiments have not come out of nowhere. “I think Japan now has the quality to reach the quarter-finals,” the head coach, Hajime Moriyasu, said. “After that, who knows if we will win or lose.”

Under Moriyasu, who has been in place since 2018, Japan have won six and drawn one of their seven European tests. After coming back from 2-0 down at home against Brazil to win 3-2 in October, a first victory against the South Americans, a win at Wembley would show that the side are the real deal. There is excitement that, after experimenting against Uruguay, England will field a strong team.

The main worry for Japan is injuries. Endo, watching from the stands at Hampden Park, is among a number of prominent absentees, having had surgery in February after injuring his ankle while in action for Liverpool, and he faces a race against time to be fit for the World Cup. Meanwhile the Anfield old boy Takumi Minamino surprised fans last week by posting a picture on social media of a treadmill run only three months after rupturing an anterior cruciate ligament. Another creative force, Takefusa Kubo of Real Sociedad, is injured. Takehiro Tomiyasu was released from his Arsenal contract last year so he could focus on getting fit after chronic problems and, after a first call-up in almost two years, the Ajax defender had to withdraw after his latest knock.

Fortunately there is strength in depth, as the Scotland game showed. Substitutes in that game, such as the Crystal Palace midfielder Daichi Kamada and the Feyenoord forward Ayase Ueda, are set to start on Tuesday, as is Mitoma, back in the blue of his country after six months away. “Against England I want us to be even more aggressive in our defending and see how much we can win the ball back,” the winger said. “In attack there may not be many chances, but I want to test the quality of those we do create.”

Coming up against some familiar defenders will not be a problem, either. “Some of the England players know me, so if they are wary of me, I think I can use that to my advantage,” Mitoma said. “Brighton supporters might come too … it’s also rare to be able to play in such a great stadium as a member of the Japanese national team.”

But no longer are Japan just happy to be here. They want to win – and confidence is high. “Until now, whenever we played against a World Cup-winning team, the expectation was that we would lose,” Moriyasu said. “Now nobody knows.”

News.title: Teacher of the Year finalist who groomed teen for sex using drugs refused to cut ties with boy even AFTER being charged
News.content:
‘PRETTY STUPID’ Teacher of the Year finalist who groomed teen for sex using drugs refused to cut ties with boy even AFTER being charged

A FINALIST for a Teacher of the Year award groomed a pupil with drugs and music, and continued messaging the teen even after being charged with felony kidnapping and sexual abuse.

Tera Johnson-Swartz, 45, from Colorado was sentenced to 14 years in prison – first for her relationship with a 16-year-old student, and then for defying a court order and continuing to contact the boy.





“She is pretty stupid, I’m not gonna lie,” the victim told police after her second arrest.



“She threw away her entire life for me”.

The former teacher at STEM School Highlands Ranch, near Denver, began texting and sharing playlists with the pupil in 2024, when the victim was just 16 years old.

She plied him with cigarettes, and let him puff on her marijuana vape pen, before they started having sex, according to court documents.

Around this time, Johnson-Swartz was named as one of seven finalists for Colorado’s Teacher of the Year award.

READ MORE ABUSE HELL I was told to strip for perv married teacher… then sick past caught up with him



Five months later in January 2025, her dark relationship with a teenage pupil was discovered and reported to the police.

She was immediately suspended, and later fired from the school and banned from the grounds.

However, less than a month later, security cams show Johnson-Swartz picking up the student from school and driving away with him.

She was charged with felony kidnapping and arrested, before being released the next day to return to court at a later date.



Johnson-Swartz then stalked the student to back-to-back concerts of one of the bands they had shared in their playlists.

The teen later told investigators: “It was really weird. I was going there expecting to have a really great time.

“And then I just see her in front of the line, like 30 feet up”

In one interview, the teen said his former teacher cornered him and said: “Just say you love me”.

The student said they were not surprised the 45-year-old struggled to stay away, saying she is an “unstable woman” who had “already ruined her life, and […] keeps just making it worse.”



The former teacher was arrested a second time, and denied bail.

Douglas County District Attorney George Brauchler said Johnson-Swartz is a “predator” who will now have to “live with that label for decades”.

News.title: I worked for the Mafia’s darkest serial killers who blowtorched privates off – I’ll never forget one madman’s sick stunt
News.content:
LOUIS Ferrante hijacked terrified truck drivers at gun point, was accused of shooting a fellow fraudster and was eventually slapped with a 13-year jail sentence after his underworld career was busted.

But, having made his name working for Mafia lords like John Gotti, his crimes paled in comparison to the madmen he played cards with and considered ‘friends’ – including a killer who blowtorched private parts.





And in many ways, the 56-year-old New Yorker is not like other gangsters.

This ‘wise guy’ was given an award in 10 Downing Street for his work with prisoners, has written several books and starred in a hit TV show.

But what really sets Big Lou apart from the other former mobsters that you see on true crime documentaries is that he never ‘snitched’ on his colleagues.

He maintained the omerta – the code of silence – rather than take a shorter prison sentence in return for providing information to the FBI back in 1996.

And while Ferrante is repentant for the torment he inflicted on his victims, he still holds ‘rats’ in contempt.

For him, it was the “treacherous” Salvatore ‘Sammy the Bull’ Gravano who almost brought down the Mafia.





Gravano, 81, only served five years in prison despite confessing to 19 murders, because he gave evidence in court against Gambino Godfather John Gotti in 1992.

It was to be the end of Gotti’s ‘Teflon Don’ reputation, with Sammy the Bull’s testimony helping send the gangster to the jail cell where he died in 2002.

Ferrante was at the home of John’s brother Pete Gotti shortly after he learned that Gravano had “gone sour” in 1991.

The gangster-turned-writer tells The Sun: “He knew that not only would it be the end of his brother but he also knew that’ll be the end of dozens of people who he had the potential to snitch on.

“It’s the moment the Mafia changed.

“That was a big turning point because all of the rats that came after always said time and again as soon as they made a deal with the government, I want a deal that’s as good as Sammy Gravano got.

“He set the precedent for a lot of the other rats to say, ‘Gee, I only killed 12 people. Why can’t I get the same five years he got? He killed 19.’

“That was a crucial moment and I was the absolute first one other than Pete to hear about it.”

Joyrider turned heist expert

Growing up in Queens in New York, Ferrante was more interested in joyriding than going to school.

It was a “fun” way of passing the time which led to far more serious crimes.



At first Ferrante sold parts from the stolen cars to backstreet repair garages, before progressing to thieving to order.

He recalls: “Instead of just stealing the cars for fun we could sell the parts. Then the body collision shops would give me an order, let’s say, ‘We need a 1989 Mercedes Benz in blue, we need parts for a 1987 Cadillac and a 1985 BMW.’ So I started to put together a crew of car thieves.”

When one of the mechanics told him how much their boxes full of tools were worth, Ferrante thought there would be more money in holding up the trucks that delivered these six-figure sum products.

Back then, he was a teenager who had no idea of the consequences of his actions, but instinctively tried to reassure the drivers whose goods he was about to unload.

Ferrante recalls: “I don’t want any of your readers to think I’m trying to say that I was nice to somebody as I was sticking a gun at their head, they’ll think I’m crazy.

“We did a bad thing but once we had him under control that’s when I said to him, ‘Look, I promise you we’ll drop you off, you’ll be fine. Is there anything in this truck you need that’s personal?’

“And he said to me, ‘There’s pictures of my family, my wife and kids, in there.’ He said, ‘Could you stick those in my pocket?’ We did.”

Serial killers

Naturally, these raids eventually caught up with Ferrante, but not before he became one of the Mafia’s go-to armed robbers.



He says: “Once you establish yourself as having a good crew that can pull off a heist and can pull off a hijack, rob a bank armoured car, once you establish yourself as a reliable crew you become extremely valuable to a Mafia family.”

Soon he found himself working for John Gotti, who took control of New York’s Gambino crime family in 1985, and other dangerous characters.

They included a hitman who took a blowtorch to the manhood of someone who had got on the wrong side of the mob.

Ferrante says: “There were a number of Mafia killers who exhibit the traits of serial killers, traits of the most perverse killers where they do things that do not need to be done.

I had friends who cut peoples’ heads off Louis Ferrante

“There are some Mafa killers who cut off penises. This particular guy, in this incident, he blowtorched someone’s penis off.

“If I was in a room with them, I got along with them. I might have played cards with them. I may have talked to them, but I wasn’t there when they did those things.

“I had friends who cut people’s heads off. Would I have a friend like that today? Absolutely not, I wouldn’t want to be anywhere near anyone who cuts people’s heads off.”

These killers let everyone know they were not to be crossed, and Ferrante will never forget one particular monster who even presented a decapitated head as a warning shot.

He continues: “Apparently he brought it to a bar and placed the head on a bar.

“I guess he wanted to show everybody whoever he had a problem with that this is what happened to my last enemy, you know, be careful what you do.”



Did the crime, did the time

Ferrante was accused of shooting another man in the leg, but his eventual convictions were for fraud and robbery.

He insists: “There’s no way I can kill somebody, especially one of my friends, somebody I know, for all the money in the world.

“That’s not to say I wasn’t capable of violence, I was. I wasn’t afraid to defend myself and my friends.”

He also would never “betray” one of his friends.

Rather than cooperate with the authorities, Ferrante pleaded guilty in 1997 to a series of robberies and was handed a 13-year prison sentence.

There’s no way I can kill somebody… That’s not to say I wasn’t capable of violence, I was Louis Ferrante

Explaining why he never informed on his fellow criminals, he says: “These are my friends. I knew their families. How do you just throw them under the bus to save yourself?”

Ferrante, who gained notoriety for rapping on a song called Justice Not Found: The John Gotti Story, is particularly aggrieved by Gravano’s duplicity.

Sammy the Bull worked his way up to become Gotti’s underboss by bumping off other gangsters.



He claims: “Sammy the Bull Gravano killed most of his victims because he wanted something from them. I didn’t like that.”

Machete murders in prison

It was going to prison that helped turn Ferrante’s life around.

When he entered the correctional facility he was “obviously illiterate” and “hadn’t picked up a book to read in my life”.

Spending days on end in his cell led him to devour books and to learn the meaning of words along the way.

Ferrante continues: “When I read those books, I understood nothing of what I read. My vocabulary wasn’t good enough to even get through a paragraph so it was confusing to me.

“Eventually I bought a dictionary in jail with stamps. I was determined to look up the definition of every single word that I did not know.”

People were killing each other with machetes Louis Ferrante

The inmate also came to feel remorse for the fear he’d brought to the world.

Ferrante says: “When I contemplated in prison I understood that there is such a thing as natural justice and karma and I was suffering from it when I was in prison.”

The maximum security prison in Lewisburg in Pennsylvania was not the place anyone would want to be.

He recalls: “People were killing each other with machetes. The Aryan Brotherhood were at war with the black Muslims and the Aryan brotherhood had hacked to death two black Muslims on the very first day I had arrived on the compound.



“People were telling me you could be targeted. I said, ‘Why? I’m Italian American.’

“They said, well, the problem is the Aryans hate you too because they hate everybody.”

Fresh start

Ferrante studied law and got his sentence reduced to eight years.

When he was released in 2003 he became an author, writing books including Mob Rules, Unlocked: The Life and Crimes of a Mafia Insider and his latest, the Borgata Trilogy.

Ferrante visited prisons, including British ones, to encourage inmates to improve their literacy.

As a result he was given a Celebrity Reading Hero Award by Sarah Brown at Downing Street.

He says: “The Brits were really good to me.”

He also promoted more cordial relations, telling prisoners that guards “want nothing more than for you to get out of here and start a better life for yourself”.

In 2013 he hosted the Discovery Channel show Inside The Gangster’s Code and has now written a history of the American Mafia.

Ferrante believes part of the reason Italians formed such tight and often violent bonds when they arrived in the United States was because they were persecuted.



He says: “I did not know until I researched for my trilogy that the Italians were the second largest ethnic group to be lynched in the United States.”

Nevertheless, prejudice does not excuse their actions, in his opinion.

Ferrante concludes: “There are plenty of Italian Americans who were discriminated against, but still chose to work hard and prospered in America.”

Lou Ferrante’s new book Borgata is released on April 7 from bookshops and Amazon.

News.title: Moment ‘drug dealer’ jumps out of dock and flees court after being told he faces jail – as manhunt launched
News.content:
THIS is the moment a suspected drug dealer jumped out the dock and fled court after being warned he faced prison.

Abu Faye, 26, was captured peeking out of the door to the courtroom before running out of shot.



He had fled Croydon Crown Court after discovering a judge wanted to remand him into custody on alleged drug offences.

The Met Police have now launched a manhunt for Faye after he fled on foot at around 4pm on March 17.



Officers said Faye, who is from Hackney, East London, has links to Penge and Cambridge.

He was charged with five counts of possession with intent to supply and five counts of possession of Class A and Class B drugs.

Faye pleaded guilty to the last five charges, which prompted the judge to try to remand him into custody.

In an appeal released today, the Met said: “Police are asking for the public’s help to trace a man who has absconded from court.



“Met detectives have been conducting urgent enquiries, including analysing CCTV, and are working at pace to locate him.

“They are now appealing to the public for help in doing so.

“If you see Faye or have any information that may assist police, please do not approach him but call 999 quoting CAD 4966/17MARCH.”

News.title: Cyprus DESERTED on Easter holidays as hotel bookings plummet 40% in wake of terrifying Iranian drone attacks on RAF base
News.content:
BRIT tourists have axed holidays in Cyprus in the wake of Iranian drone attacks – with the island’s hotel bookings plunging by 40 per cent.

Shocking photos showed streets and beaches deserted over Easter – just weeks after the terrifying strike on RAF Akrotiri amid the Middle East war.





The US-Israeli campaign against the Iranian regime kicked off on February 28 with the assassination of Ali Khamenei – just as Cyprus was restarting its tourism industry after winter.

On March 1, as waves of Iranian drones were launched across the region, the runway on Brit base RAF Akrotiri was blitzed by a UAV fired by the rogue state.

The attack sparked a series of holiday cancellations – with the spiralling Iran war already triggering travel chaos across the Middle East.

There has been a staggering 40 per cent drop in March bookings and a ​similar loss in April, Cyprus’ Hoteliers Association said.

Brit travellers usually make up a third of arrivals in Cyprus – with island welcoming four million international visitors last year.

The latest sharp decline in bookings has dealt a huge blow to Cyprus’ local economy.

Short-term rental cancellation rates also soared from around 15 per cent to 100 per cent following the outbreak of conflict, according to AirDNA.



The costs have since settled from their all-time spike, but remained at about 45 per cent on March 21.

Nearby nations including Greece and Turkey have also seen cancellation rate increases – as the entire region’s tourism industry continues to suffer.

Haunting images have also shown empty streets across other holiday hotspots including Dubai – which has seen a social media crackdown on images and video of the destruction.

Muskita Hotels, a firm that operates three hotels in Cyprus, told the Financial Times said it had seen a spate of cancellations for trips in March and April.

Meanwhile, EasyJet chief executive Kenton Jarvis told the outlet: “If you look at a map of Europe, we saw obviously a drop in demand in Cyprus and Turkey and that side of Africa.”



The cost of accommodation in April and May in Cyprus also plummeted by 12 per cent comparing last week to the one before the start of the war, Lighthouse Intelligence reported.

Beaches in Cyprus – including popular areas like Protaras and Limassol, have been noticeably quieter than usual.

Visitors have recorded striking footage of abandoned streets as the war continues to show no signs of slowing.



It comes after the Iranian drone strike on RAF Akrotiri earlier this month – which raised fears over Britain’s air defence capabilities.

The horror attack also sparked a response from the UK – as Britain moved to deploy HMS Dragon to Cyprus.

The warship took three weeks to arrive at its destination after it was scrambled from dry dock into action.

The Middle East war has now hit the one-month mark – as talks between the US and Iran continue.

Donald Trump on Monday declared “great progress” in crunch peace talks with the reeling regime.



The US president said a deal will “probably” come soon but warned he’ll unleash total “obliteration” otherwise.

In a fiery post on Truth Social, Trump said America is now in “serious discussions” with what he called a “new and more reasonable” regime in Tehran.

He hailed “great progress” and said a deal will “probably” be reached soon.



But he made it crystal clear the stakes couldn’t be higher.

Don warned that if Iran fails to agree – and if the Strait of Hormuz is not “immediately ‘Open for Business’”– the US will respond with overwhelming force.

He said America will conclude its “lovely ‘stay’ in Iran by blowing up and completely obliterating all of their Electric Generating Plants, Oil Wells and Kharg Island (and possibly all desalinization plants!), which we have purposefully not yet ‘touched’.”

Trump added the strikes would come in retaliation for US troops killed during what he called Iran’s 47-year “Reign of Terror.”

The explosive warning comes as Trump ramps up pressure on the battered Iranian regime, with US forces already hammering thousands of targets and closing in on a final blow.



Around 10,000 US troops – including elite Marines and paratroopers from the 83rd Airborne – are being surged into the region.

And warships like the USS Tripoli, carrying 3,500 personnel, are already in position.

Behind the scenes, the US leader has also floated a bold plan to seize Iran’s oil lifeline in a move that would cripple the regime’s ability to bankroll terror.



At the centre is Kharg Island – the key export terminal where most of Iran’s crude flows out.

Trump told the Financial Times: “To be honest with you, my favourite thing is to take the oil in Iran but some stupid people back in the US say: ‘why are you doing that?’ But they’re stupid people.”

He added: “Maybe we take Kharg Island, maybe we don’t. We have a lot of options.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Trump has set an April 6 deadline, with devastating strikes on Iran’s energy sector ready to go if talks collapse.

News.title: Hilarious moment beauty pageant contestant Darathorn Yoothong busts into wild swimsuit dance – earning her viral fame
News.content:
THIS is the hysterical moment a beauty pageant contestant bursts into a high-energy dance – thrusting her into the spotlight.

Footage shows Darathorn Yoothong frantically dancing in the preliminary rounds of the Miss Grand Thailand competition.





Wearing nothing but a swimsuit, she quickly captures the attention of thousands watching online.

The 18-year-old shows off her aggressive, hip-hop dance moves without any concern for what people think.

Her fellow contestants can do nothing but watch on as she dominates the stage.

Unfortunately, it wasn’t enough for Yoothong to take home first prize.



She finished inside the top 20, but her performance instantly became one of the most recognisable moments from this year’s competition.

A clip of Yoothong’s routine went viral on social media with one user commenting: “God forbid a girl does what she likes.”

Another wrote: “She genuinely looks fun to be with – she is the party.”

Yoothong competed as Miss Grand Kalasin, representing one of 77 provinces in the national pageant.



With choreographed gestures and exaggerated expressions, her dance has since been labelled the “Kalasin Strut”.

The overall winner, Pattama Jitsawat, will go on to represent Thailand at the Miss Grand International competition in India later this year.

However, this is not the only notable moment from this year’s competition.

In a separate category, contestant Kamolwan Chanago’s teeth fell out while delivering her opening remarks.

Rather than running offstage, Chanago simply turned her back to the audience to fix her pearly whites back into position.



Impressed by her bravery, the audience then began to cheer.

Spurred on by the applause, Chanago then completed the rest of her routine, even mustering a smile for the camera.

Video of the remarkable incident quickly went viral on social media, with users praising her professionalism.

In November, Miss Universe winner Victoria Theilvig led a mass walkout from a star-studded event in Bangkok.

The 21-year-old beauty queen stormed out in solidarity with Miss Mexico after the pageant president publicly reprimanded her on camera.



Nawat Itsaragrisil, Vice President for Asia and Oceania within the Miss Universe Organisation, berated contestant Melissa Flores Bosch for missing a sponsor shoot earlier that day.

During a live-stream, Nawat confronted Bosch and asked her to “explain herself” in front of the cameras.

When Bosch pushed back, he told her: “I didn’t give you the opportunity to talk.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I have a voice,” Bosch replied, accusing him of “not respecting me as a woman.”

The highly-publicised walkout has reignited criticism of the Miss Universe Organisation over transparency and contestant treatment.

News.title: I spent £1,500 doing up my driveway only for council to say I CAN’T use it due to ridiculous parking ‘rule’
News.content:
PARKED OFF I spent £1,500 doing up my driveway only for council to say I CAN’T use it due to ridiculous parking ‘rule’

A MAN who spent over £1000 on a new driveway has been left crushed after the local council rejected his application for a dropped kerb.

The application is necessary to ensure his driveway is legal to use.



Jonathan Parkin’s request to the council to drop the adjacent pavement kerb was rejected after building a £1500 driveway extension.



The planning permission application – which costs £165 – was rejected on the grounds that a dropped kerb would take up too much street parking.

This came as a shock to Parkin, whose surrounding neighbours had their requests approved.

Speaking to the Daily Echo, Parkin said: “If they refuse your application they should give you your money back at least.

“They just said no and that was the end of that, I feel very frustrated that nobody would even come out.

“The only people that park outside the house are my family and friends.”

Parkin owns an electrical company, and does not want to leave his tools on the street in view overnight.

A private driveway would also offer cheaper car insurance as they would be parked on private property.

The extension, intended to hold three cars, is currently not legal to use without the dropped kerb.



A Southampton City Council Spokesperson said: “The council must carefully consider the long‑term impact of removing on‑street parking spaces when assessing dropped kerb applications as on street parking can be utilised by all residents, visitors, and deliveries.

“In line with the council’s dropped crossing policy, vehicle crossings are required to be kept to a minimum width.

“Where a proposed new crossing or extension would result in the loss of a full on‑street parking space, the application will not normally be approved.

“All dropped kerb applications are assessed on a case‑by‑case basis to ensure the policy is applied fairly and proportionately, taking into account local parking conditions and highway safety considerations.”

This comes after a Dorset couple have been forced to rip down a garden fence installed for privacy after failing to obtain planning permission.



Paul and Lisa Toomer bought their £1.15m house five years ago but became concerned about security after a spate of attempted burglaries in the area.

They then erected a two metre fence at the bottom of their garden, thinking they were within their rights under permitted development.

The local council then paid them a visit, stating the fence to be unregulated and “ugly”.

They then ordered the couple to tear the fence down.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The couple have filed a number of appeals, and are currently waiting on an appeal to the most recent enforcement notice.



They are still waiting for a date to be set for the appeal decision.

News.title: Air Canada CEO to quit after outrage over LaGuardia crash that killed two pilots – because he didn’t say sorry in FRENCH
News.content:
THE CEO of Air Canada has been forced to step down after not saying sorry in French following a horror crash that killed two pilots.

Michael Rousseau sparked mass controversy by issuing an English-only video message with French subtitles to express condolences after the collision between an Air Canada jet and a fire truck in New York.





The incident killed pilots, Antoine Forest and Mackenzie Gunther, and injured 41 people who were taken to hospital.

He expressed his “deepest sorrow for everyone affected” in the disaster – but he only words he said in French were “bonjour” and “merci.”

Rousseau later issued a written apology over his English-only message, this time in both languages.

He said he was “deeply saddened” that his lack of language skills “diverted attention” away from the victims’ families and Air Canada staffers involved in the crash.

“Despite many lessons over several years, unfortunately, I am still unable to express myself adequately in French,” he said in a statement.

He added: “I sincerely apologise for this, but I am continuing my efforts to improve.”

As part of the criticism, people pointed out that Forest was from French-speaking Quebec.

Canada has two official languages – English and French – and many people in high-ranking positions are expected to speak both.



Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney was one of the people who hit out at Rousseau’s conduct, saying he was “very disappointed, as others are, rightly so, in this unilingual message.”

Carney added that the message showed a “lack of judgement and a lack of compassion.”

Similarly, Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand stressed he should speak both official languages.

“Canada is a bilingual country,” she said.

Quebec Premier Francois Legault was also among those who called for the CEO’s resignation.



He pointed out that when Rousseau was appointed president of the airline in February 2021, he promised to learn French.

Announcing his retirement, he said: “It has been my great honour to work with the dedicated and talented people of Air Canada and to represent our outstanding organisation.

“I look forward to supporting our company during this important transition period.”

As the PR crisis reaches a peak, victims of the crash are still recovering from their horror injuries in hospital.

Air Canada crew member, Solange Tremblay, was hurled more than 320 feet across the runway when crash happened.



The impact reportedly catapulted the stewardess from the wreckage, leaving rescuers to discover her lying on the tarmac – still strapped into her jump seat.

Her daughter Sarah Lepine described the terrifying moment in a GoFundMe appeal set up to help with her mum’s medical treatment.

She wrote: “During the crash she was… ejected over 320 feet from the wreckage.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“She was found still strapped in her jump seat lying on the tarmac.”

Despite her devastating injuries, Lepine said her mum surviving the crash was “a total miracle”.

News.title: Shocking moment runaway truck FLIPS crushing car as it narrowly avoids desperate workers trying to stop it
News.content:
THIS is the tense moment a huge truck suddenly rolls backwards and flips over – narrowly missing a panicked worker.

The truck was being loaded with boxes on Rua Tacoativa in São Paulo, Brazil when the brakes gave out and its huge bulk began to move backwards, nearly crushing the two workers behind it.





The nail-biting footage shows the truck rolling backwards down a steep street and quickly gaining speed, before hitting the first parked car and then overturning onto a second vehicle.

Two workers try in vain to stop the truck as it begins moving but they jump away moments before it crashes and flips.

A pedestrian on the opposite pavement was also nearly hit, and can be seen in the video running from the scene.

Onlookers anxiously watched as the truck collision partially flipped up another car and sent boxes flying, causing complete carnage.

There was also another worker still inside the vehicle when it began moving, but shortly after the truck had flipped and crushed the bonnet of a nearby car, he jumped out of the back, seemingly unharmed.

Luckily, no one was injured during the double-vehicle-flip accident, and only material goods were damaged.

It follows after a remarkably lucky escape for one Japanese potato vendor whose truck caught fire and was flaming down the highway as he drove himself to the fire station.



The potato vendor truck was engulfed in flames, blasting disco music as it and running through red lights at high speed in the streets of Kumamoto City.

Onlookers watched aghast at the fiery spectacle and filmed the incident for social media.

Though the truck was burnt to a crisp, leaving behind only a charred skeleton, the elderly driver survived unharmed.

One commenter on X quipped: “Japanese society is so civilized that the fires simply drive themselves to the fire station.”

News.title: Top 10 most awkward moments in life leaving Brits embarrassed
News.content:
Top 10 most awkward moments in life leaving Brits embarrassed

A new survey has revealed the top ten most awkward moments that leave Brits feeling uncomfortable

View 2 Images Brits have been left red in the face after texting the wrong person (Image: Getty Images)

According to research, some of the most uncomfortable moments in life include calling someone by the wrong name and falling over in public. Polling suggests that 37% of UK adults frequently experience embarrassing or awkward encounters, with many noting that the nation as a whole is prone to these uncomfortable moments.

‌



A survey of 2,000 adults revealed that having a growling stomach in a quiet room full of people (32%) and accidentally getting into the wrong car (21%) are also considered highly mortifying experiences. Additionally, sending a message to the wrong group chat (31%) was cited as another particularly uncomfortable moment.

‌



View 2 Images Running and missing a bus is considered one of the most embarrassing moments (Image: Getty Images)

‌



For 40% of Gen Z, trying to grab somebody’s attention and being ignored is the most awkward and uncomfortable thing that can happen, with 19% most likely to pretend it never did. But 21% of Millennials consider greeting someone with the wrong handshake the worst of the bunch.

The research was commissioned by Samsung to mark the launch of Galaxy Buds4 Pro, which are designed to adjust to real‑world conditions and everyday situations by automatically adjusting volume and noise-cancelling depending on external factors.

‌



For 48% having earbuds nearby after an awkward moment provides a welcome sense of comfort. Four in ten also revealed they find it easier to get through uncomfortable situations when wearing them.

It emerged women were likely to find tripping up most embarrassing (47%), whereas men put calling someone the wrong name as top of their troubles (45%).

But more than one in five will laugh at themselves when an embarrassing moment occurs. Another 49% will make a self‑deprecating joke and move on, while 12% double down confidently, pretending the faux pas was intentional.

Article continues below

Nearly half (49%) admitted they can let it go when they know it’ll make for a good story later. They also admit these moments can feel worse when in unfamiliar company.

A fifth added that an uncomfortable incident usually sticks with them for only a few minutes, but one in ten claimed it lingers for 'several days'.

THE TOP 10 MOST AWKWARD MOMENTS IN LIFE:

News.title: Do 1 simple thing before moving to keep important documents safe
News.content:
Do 1 simple thing before moving to keep important documents safe

Brit are being urged to take one simple step before moving house to make sure they keep important documents safe

View 2 Images Moving house can be a stressful process and misplacing items can make it even worse (Image: Getty Images)

Chargers, clothes and furniture screws are the most common things people lose in a house move. A poll of 1,000 adults who have moved house in the last five years found 14% ended up shelling out more than £150 to replace lost belongings. Other commonly misplaced items included books (26%) or single socks and shoes (21%). Meanwhile, 52% admitted to breaking an average of four items while moving, costing them £82 each time.

‌



The research was commissioned by the HMRC app which has teamed up with moving firm Pickfords to help customers stay on top of important admin during stressful moments like moving house.

‌



View 2 Images Important documents can easily get lost if not properly stored away (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Sarah McMann, chief digital product owner, for the app said: “Moving home can be stressful, there’s a lot to keep on top of and it’s easy for important documents to get lost along the way.

“We can help ease that pressure by keeping your tax information safe, secure and easy to access.”

The study found important documents are what people are most worried about losing when moving house (59%) – outranking those worried about losing electronics or furniture – with most people worried about losing their passports, birth certificates and driver’s licenses.

‌



Nearly nine in 10 of those polled find moving home stressful, with the physical move being the worst part for 51%, while another 38% dread having to update their new address.

A further 75% say the process of moving feels chaotic and rushed, with 80% saying an app to help track important documents would make the process easier, according to the OnePoll.com figures.

‌



The study found 29% of those who have moved took over three weeks to update their address details with key institutions such as bands, utilities and doctor’s surgeries.

Which may be due to only 63% being confident they could even find their key documents quickly after making a house move.

TOP 20 THINGS PEOPLE LOSE WHEN MOVING HOUSE:

Chargers Screws needed to reassemble furniture Clothing Books One sock or shoe Tools TV remote Jewellery Toiletries Photographs Small appliances like hairdryer or kettle Gardening equipment Financial documents Money Reading glasses Wall clocks Game controllers Family heirlooms Passport Furniture

News.title: Keir Starmer sends urgent Iran war message to business chiefs as he warns of 'duty' to Brits
News.content:
Keir Starmer sends urgent Iran war message to business chiefs as he warns of 'duty' to Brits

Keir Starmer has told business chiefs it must be a 'joint effort' in tackling the impact of the Iran war as he said there is a 'duty to protect British citizens'

View 2 Images The Prime Minister hosted energy and shipping bosses in Downing Street (Image: PA)

Keir Starmer has told business chiefs it must be a “joint effort” in tackling the impact of the Iran war as he said there is a “duty to protect British citizens” from being clobbered by rising costs.

‌



The Prime Minister hosted energy and shipping bosses in Downing Street on Monday where he said he is working on a "viable plan" for the Strait of Hormuz.

‌



Tehran’s blockade of the crucial shipping route - which transports around a fifth of the world's oil and gas - has sent energy prices spiralling. Mr Starmer said one option to tackle Iran’s chokehold is a “military” plan, while another is a 35-country coalition which is trying to de-escalate the war and “find a way forward”.

‌



The PM said his priority was addressing British families’ concerns about bills soaring. At the start of the meeting, he told business leaders: "This is going to have to be a joint effort. The Government can't do it on its own. You can't do it on your own. We're going to have to work together on this, which is why I want to have a conversation here this afternoon."

View 2 Images Business chiefs were told it must be a 'joint effort' with the Government to tackle the impact of the Iran war (Image: Getty Images)

He continued: “It's not our war but it is our duty to protect British citizens, particularly their concern will be not just the escalation of the war, but this sense that it's going to hit them and their families and their households.

‌



“And I think probably uppermost in their minds at the moment is energy bills, petrol and also food prices. On household energy bills, as you've probably seen, we've already taken action for the time being, and therefore this Wednesday, household energy bills will go down by just over £100 on average and then stay down until the end of June, whatever happens in the conflict.

Attendees at the No10 meeting included bosses from Shell and BP, shipping giant Maersk, maritime insurance specialist Lloyd's of London and banks HSBC and Goldman Sachs.

The US-Israeli war with Iran has driven up global energy prices dramatically and sparked fears of potential shortages of petrol. The blockade could also impact food supplies due to the impact on shipments of fertiliser from Gulf countries.

‌



Speaking about action to tackle the blockade on the Strait of Hormuz, Mr Starmer said: “Firstly, we've been bringing together a sort of coalition of countries around the notion that we do have to de-escalate and find a way forward.

“Now we've started that with the sort of key European countries, the so-called E4 which is Germany, Italy, France and the United Kingdom, but we now got about 35 countries that are signed up to that. So that is good. And we are also working on a sort of military level of what a viable plan would actually look like.”

Earlier today, Mr Starmer also criticised opposition leaders’ position on the conflict, saying: “If you took Kemi Badenoch or Nigel Farage. What did they want to do? They wanted to go straight in with both feet into the war without thinking through the consequences. They are in opposition at the moment - maybe that doesn't matter very much.”

‌



The PM is set to hold a Cobra meeting on Tuesday to discuss the impact on the cost of living.

Meanwhile, Chancellor Rachel Reeves joined a virtual meeting of G7 finance and energy ministers and central bank governors, along with Energy Secretary Ed Miliband. The G7 - the UK, US, Germany, France, Italy, Canada and Japan along with the European Union - considered ways to respond to the economic hit from the war.

Defence Secretary John Healey is in the Middle East to speak to the UK's allies in the Gulf.

Article continues below

US president Donald Trump has threatened the destruction of Iran's energy infrastructure and possibly its water desalination plants unless the Strait is "open for business". The Prime Minister has urged for de-escalation in the Middle East, but the US President has sent thousands of extra US troops and raised the prospect of military action to seize Iran's Kharg Island, a crucial facility for oil exports.

The cost of oil benchmark Brent crude lifted more than 3% to 117 dollars a barrel at one stage in Monday morning trading, reaching levels not seen since 2022. Diesel prices have reached their most expensive level since December 2022, with the average price of a litre of the fuel at UK forecourts on Monday hitting 181.2p according to RAC analysis.

News.title: Manchester counter terror incident LIVE as armed police block off street
News.content:
Specialist counter-terror police have been scrambled and undercover vehicles have responded to an incident.

Officers were pictured pointing guns towards a building in Bury, Greater Manchester this afternoon.

News.title: 'I clashed with Farage in US - he's only interested in one thing', top Congressman warns
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: 'I clashed with Farage in US - he's only interested in one thing', top Congressman warns

Speaking to the Mirror at his Congressional Office in Washington DC this week, Rep. Jamie Raskin gave a stern warning to British voters not to fall for 'imposter' Nigel Farage

British voters shouldn't fall for "charlatan" Nigel Farage- Senior US congressman has warned

British voters shouldn't fall for "charlatan" Nigel Farage like Americans did for Donald Trump, a senior US congressman has warned.

‌



Jamie Raskin, the leading Democrat in the House Judiciary Committee, clashed with Mr Farage during a visit to the UK last summer. And he launched a furious attack on the the Reform leader when he visited Washington to give evidence to his committee on "free speech" issues last September.

‌



Speaking to the Mirror at his Congressional Office in Washington DC, he gave a stern warning to British voters not to fall for "imposter" Farage.

‌



"He doesn't have a free speech bone in his body," Rep. Raskin told the Mirror. "He's only interested in advancing right wing politics."

Mirror confronts Liz Truss over bid to become Britain's Donald Trump READ MORE :

View Image Rep. Jamie Raskin issued a warning to voters not to fall for Nigel Farage (Image: Getty Images)

Asked if the UK could be following down the same track as Trump's America, he added: "You're looking at a guy who grew up on Shakespeare and The Clash and I'm somebody who believes in British political culture and music.

‌



"The Beatles and the Rolling Stones, I cannot imagine a society that produces some of the greatest writing, and amazing poets and amazing musicians, could fall for a free speech impostor and charlatan like that.

"I don't think that's going to happen. I want to make the UK great again by getting back to your roots."

He added: "So much of our humanity has been written by people in the UK. I cannot imagine Brits falling for a fraud like that, or anybody who would view Donald Trump as their role model."

‌



Rep. Raskin recounted his first fiery showdown with Farage, which took place in London last July.

"I met him originally when we were over in the UK," he said. "We were having what was supposed to be a conversation about free speech in Europe and in America.

"And the way we do it here in Congress is the majority gets its turn, then the minority gets its turn. So, Chairman [Republican Congressman Jim] Jordan started off with questioning of various witnesses, including Nigel Farage.

Article continues below

"And then it was our turn, and so they went for about an hour. And then I began on our behalf, and within two or three minutes, Nigel Farage didn't like what he was hearing because I was actually talking about the state of free speech in America.

"And he began to rant and rave, and then, like a little boy taking home his football because he doesn't like what's happening on the field, he said.

"This is over. I'm going to cancel this." And you know, he demonstrated perfectly there exactly what his attitude is about free speech."

News.title: Car 'mounted pavement outside packed bar' in Derby and what unfolded was horrific
News.content:
Car 'mounted pavement outside packed bar' in Derby and what unfolded was horrific

A black Suzuki Swift vehicle ended up colliding with people enjoying a drink with friends, venue boss Calum Green said. The ‘horrific’ incident happened right outside his bar Bishop Blaise on Friar Gate.

View 4 Images Police forensic officers at Derby crash scene (Image: Emma Trimble / SWNS)

The driver of a car which ploughed into a crowd injuring seven people in Derby had mounted the pavement outside a packed bar, the boss said today. The black Suzuki Swift vehicle ended up colliding with people enjoying a drink with friends, Calum Green said. The ‘horrific’ incident happened right outside his bar Bishop Blaise on Friar Gate. He told how staff members heard a commotion and ran outside to try to help injured people. Speaking as his venue reopened, he said: ‘It was a busy Saturday night as usual with lots of revellers out and about. ‘What unfolded was horrific.

‌



View 4 Images Drone image of the scene of the crash in Derby (Image: Emma Trimble / SWNS)

‌



Counter terror police assist probe into Derby city centre car rampage READ MORE :

Derby police issue major update after Suzuki Swift driven into Friar Gate revellers READ MORE :

As police continued to question a 36-year-old male, of Indian origin, on suspicion of attempted murder, Mr Green, 29, said the car ‘clearly mounted the kerb and pavement once’ . He said: "‘It has left locals very shocked and shaken.’ The leader of Derby City Council, Nadine Peatfield, speaking as she visited the scene, told how the busy street, packed with bars and restaurants, would be subjected to a traffic ban over the long Easter weekend. She said: ‘I am absolutely horrified by what happened and my heart goes out to everyone injured and witnesses who saw it. ‘It is just horrific.’

‌



View 4 Images Chief Superintendent Emma Aldred at the scene of the incident in Derby (Image: Emma Trimble / SWNS)

She outlined how the council has set up a recovery group to help ‘reassure people over the weekend and with no vehicles travelling up or down Friar Gate.’ She added: ‘It is a busy place for people to congregate at night and locals may feel vulnerable in this small city. ‘But police are saying this is an isolated incident. We are working with them and will have an extra presence over the Bank Holiday weekend.’

The incident occurred at about 9.30pm on Saturday. Police stopped a suspect seven minutes later and two miles away. Two people have been discharged from hospital after they were among seven people hit by a car in Derby city centre.

‌



View 4 Images Debris left at the scene of the incident in Derby (Image: Emma Trimble / SWNS)

Their discharge comes as detectives received more time to question a man arrested on suspicion of attempted murder after the car injured the group in Friar Gate at 9.30pm on Saturday.

The police cordon around the scene is expected to be lifted for businesses this morning.

‌



Claire Ward, mayor of the East Midlands, called for local communities and agencies to do "all we can" to support people affected, adding that two people have now been released from hospital.

Derbyshire Police said it was continuing to question a 36-year-old Derby man, who was originally from India, after being given more time to hold him in custody.

Counter-terrorism police have joined the investigation but Derbyshire Police said this was "common practice for an incident of this nature".

‌



Officers were "keeping an open mind about the potential motives."

The suspect is also being held on suspicion of causing serious injury through dangerous driving, inflicting grievous bodily harm with intent and dangerous driving.

Police are not currently treating the incident as terrorism.

News.title: The 'super' foster mum and dad who have cared for 336 children over 50 years
News.content:
The 'super' foster mum and dad who have cared for 336 children over 50 years

Michael, 78, and Marilyn, 74, from Rochdale in Greater Manchester are celebrating five decades as foster parents. A local newspaper ad placed by Rochdale Borough Council first caught their eye in 1976. The couple have since cared for 336 children and have no plans to stop their life long caring just yet

View 4 Images Super foster parents Michael and Marilyn receiving their award

A loving couple are celebrating 50 years as foster parents, with no plans to retire after caring for 336 children.

‌



Michael, 78, and Marilyn, 74, from Rochdale in Greater Manchester are celebrating five decades as foster parents.

‌



A local newspaper  placed by Rochdale Borough Council first caught their eye in 1976.

‌



The couple have since cared for 336 children and have no plans to stop their life long caring just yet.

"I would really miss it," said Marilyn, who did not want to give her full name, after being recognised by Rochdale Council.

Michael added: "We feel privileged and proud." The couple, married for five years with two young children, began fostering fifty years ago.

‌



View 4 Images Michael and Marilyn are still going strong after 50 years of fostering

They heard the local authority was looking for foster carers who could look after very young babies.

‌



They "knew straight away" that another child would "fit right in" at their home And, 330 children later, they are still going strong.

Marilyn knew it was right for them right from that very first adoption all those years ago.

“It was lovely to have another little one about, I loved it," she recalled.

‌



“She was about 2 days old when she came to us, and we had her for 2 and a half months.

“I can still remember sitting in our living room, the night before she left us at the end of her placement, crying and thinking, ‘What am I going to do without this baby?' “So, it snowballed from there and now we probably care for 4 or 5 children a year.”

Michael jokingly recalled the sleepless nights and nighttime feeds but said how it ‘has become a part of their life’, with 4 hours of sleep fairly common for the pair. In their early years as foster carers, Michael and Marilyn were still growing their own family; one child in their care moved in with their adoptive parents just a month before Marilyn gave birth to their third child.

‌



The pair eventually had children of their own and are now grandparents to 13.

View 4 Images Michael and Marilyn are still going strong after 50 years of fostering

The most children they have cared for at one time in their roles is five, including several siblings. They often receive a call from their adoptive family, saying, ‘We’re coming to Rochdale, can we come and see you?’, which they love to hear. Michael said: “Some of them just want a cuddle from Marilyn. She’s like a mother to them; that’s the kind of thing that can be missing in their lives.” Some of the children brought their own children too. Marilyn added: “We’ve been to weddings, adoption parties, christenings, 18th and 21st birthday parties. It’s lovely when you think about starting with them as a baby and now they’ve grown. “We’ve had letters from adoptive parents saying, ‘They’ve turned out like they have because of you,’ which is nice.” Celebrating their 50-year fostering anniversary, the couple, who have also been married for 55 years, had afternoon tea with the Mayor of Rochdale, Councillor Janet Emsley, at Rochdale Town Hall. They received a mayoral recognition award in honour of their long-standing commitment to fostering and for being some of the UK’s longest serving foster carers.

‌



View 4 Images Rochdale in the 1950s, when the couple started fostering (Image: Mirrorpix)

Anyone over the age of 21 with a spare room in their home, like Marilyn and Michael, can become a foster carer and support those most in need. Councillor Rachel Massey, cabinet member for children’s services and education, said: “Michael and Marilyn are an extraordinary example of the love, stability and care that foster carers bring into a child’s life. “Their dedication over the last 50 years has transformed the futures of hundreds of children and young people and they are living proof that what matters most is kindness, patience and willingness to open your home and heart to a child who needs it.

“We are incredibly grateful for everything they have done for our borough’s children and for the inspiration they continue to provide to others."” *Visit www.fosterforgm.com/Rochdale or call 0300 303 0321 for further information on fostering.

News.title: Brit drivers urged to fill up on petrol and diesel before 10am on Thursday
News.content:
Brit drivers urged to fill up on petrol and diesel before 10am on Thursday

The RAC warns nearly 21 million leisure trips are planned over the holiday period, with coastal routes likely to be hit hardest and multiple UK motorways set for heavy congestion this week

View 2 Images Brits have been warned to fill up as soon as possible (Image: Huchot-Boissier Patricia/ABACA/Shutterstock)

Drivers have been urged to set off early ahead of a bumper Easter getaway, with more cars expected on the roads than at any point in the past four years.

‌



The Royal Automobile Club warns nearly 21 million leisure trips are planned over the holiday period. Coastal routes are likely to be hit hardest, according to the AA, with the M4, M25, M5, M40 and M1 all set for heavy congestion this week.

‌



Despite rising fuel prices - driven by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East - most motorists won't be changing their plans. RAC research shows that while 31% of drivers are increasingly concerned about costs, the majority still intent to travel.

‌



RAC mobile servicing and repairs team leader Sean Kimberlin has advised drivers to fill up and set off on their journeys as soon as possible - definitely before 10am on Thursday.

View 2 Images Fuel prices have surged amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East

‌



He said: "Fuel prices may have risen sharply in recent weeks, but our research with drivers shows they are still determined to make the most of the Easter break.

"Despite diesel costing around £19 more per tank than last year and petrol about £8 more, only a small number of people are actually changing their plans. For many, Easter is the first real chance to get away since Christmas, so we’re urging drivers to use the myRAC app to find the cheapest forecourts near them."

He added: "This year we’re expecting one of the busiest Easter getaways since 2022, with planned leisure trips rising again for the second year running.

Article continues below

"Traffic is likely to build from Thursday as schools break up, with the M5 towards Devon and Cornwall and the M25 set to be particularly congested. The worst delays are expected from around 10am, so getting on the road early is still the best way to avoid the queues."

Fuel prices have surged across the globe as the key trade route through the Strait of Hormuz remains a contentious point in the war with Iran. The waterway conveys about 20% of the world's oil and gas.

Boxing.title: 'A nose bleed in the ring saved my life': Rising star REUBEN MUSTON reveals his extraordinary journey since a rare illness nearly killed him - and how he became the first pro boxer to fight after having a stem cell transplant
Boxing.content:
'A nose bleed in the ring saved my life': Rising star REUBEN MUSTON reveals his extraordinary journey since a rare illness nearly killed him - and how he became the first pro boxer to fight after having a stem cell transplant

Fighting for money doesn’t hold nearly the same fear as fighting for your life. Reuben Muston is better placed than most to make the distinction.

‘I’m just happy to be here,’ he says, and it’s a summary that serves only a modicum of justice to a remarkable tale.

You see, Muston became a professional boxer this month, which is common enough. But where his situation differs is the background - no British fighter before him has crossed to the paid ranks after undergoing a stem cell transplant.

He will explain the gravity and science behind that situation in his own words. And why he would most likely be dead if it wasn’t for a nosebleed that ran for the better part of five days.

But to get there, Muston first goes back to February 12, 2022 and a leisure centre in Barnsley. It was the semi-final of the England Youth Championships and Muston, a lad of 17 from Reading and one of the country’s best amateur flyweights, was up against Mikie Tallon. Big fight, big opportunity.

‘I was quite clearly up on the scorecards but towards the end of the second round, we clash heads,’ says Muston. ‘I go back to the corner and there is blood everywhere from my nose.

'I'm just happy to be here,' says boxer Reuben Muston (pictured with his dad Danny), three years on from the pair's stem cell transplant that saved his life

Former world champion Anthony Crolla is one of the informed cohort of observers who believe Muston could make waves in the sport

‘The third round, it’s still bleeding. OK. Well, the ref stops us a couple of times, gets the doctor to take a look and then, with about 30 seconds left, he tells me, “I can't let you go on any more”. Honestly, the ring, me and Mikie were covered in blood.

‘It shattered my heart. That championship was meant to be my break and I’m devastated. So I go home that night and for some reason my nose is still bleeding. Bleeding on me, my dinner, everything. It hadn’t stopped by the time I went to bed.’

As it transpires, packing his nose with tissue wasn’t the solution. Muston recalls: ‘When I got up it was like a murder scene – blood all over my sheets, all up the walls.

‘My dad took one look at me and said we’re going to A&E. They did hours of tests and after a while a doctor took us to a private room. They suspected it might be leukaemia, but under the microscope it didn’t look how it should.’

That meant more tests. Many of them. Across the span of three days, specialists of all denominations came and went. While this was happening, the bleeding did not stop.

Eventually, one of the tests, a biopsy on his bone marrow, zeroed in on a reason - aplastic anaemia. Exceptionally rare, it’s a life-threatening blood disorder that causes the marrow to stop producing enough new blood cells and affects between two and six people per million. Muston was exceptionally unlucky, save for one fact – the good fortune of a nosebleed that led to the diagnosis.

Muston: ‘The most basic way of explaining it is what I was told. So your platelet count should be between 150,000 and 400,000 (per microlitre) and your haemoglobin should be between 120 and 150 (per litre of blood) but I had a platelet count of 1,000 and my haemoglobin was 55. Below 50 and you can go into cardiac arrest.

‘The doctors said, “In two weeks, you could have had a massive brain haemorrhage or cardiac arrest and you would have been dead”, essentially. Really, the nosebleed saved my life.’

After days of tests, Muston was eventually diagnosed with aplastic anaemia - a rare blood disorder that affects just two to six people in every million

‘The doctors said, “In two weeks, you could have had a massive brain haemorrhage or cardiac arrest and you would have been dead”'

It did. But the first challenge of this second chance was finding a stem cell donor. Plans to go to university were parked, boxing was impossible, and Muston instead joined the Anthony Nolan stem cell register, searching for a match.

‘We started hoping for anyone who would be a 10 out of 10 match, but we found two people who were a nine out of 10, one of them in Brazil. After further testing, we saw they couldn’t match us.

‘We tried everything. My mum has a rare bone marrow type where only a couple of hundred people in the world could match. My dad’s was even rarer, but he was a five out of 10 match for mine. In the end we decided that was the best option.’

After five days of chemotherapy to prepare his body, Muston received the stem cell transplant from his father, Dan, three years ago today. Despite uncomfortable odds, it worked.

The next year was spent on a regimen of 40 pills a day, two to three blood transfusions a week, and almost total isolation at home to shield from infection, with the lingering fear that ‘a common cold could kill me’. He would ultimately sit his A-levels at the dining room table and went jogging only when he felt up to it, but precisely 12 months after going into isolation, he ran the London Marathon.

Today, those strides have extended to a place that once seemed highly unlikely. Or impossible, based on one of the first conversations Muston had soon after his diagnosis.

‘I remember I was three weeks away from boxing for an English title and my first question was whether I would box again,’ he says. ‘He looked at me and went, “No, I don't see it”. That was really hard to take, but I wasn’t going to give up.’

Muston has had 12 fights since his transplant, winning 10 of them and collecting two national titles

'Three years after the transplant, I’m feeling good. This whole time has really taught me I didn't know about myself, about how deep I can dig'

Since his transplant and recovery, Muston has had 12 fights, won 10, and collected two national titles. Frank Warren is among the promoters with whom he is discussing his professional career; the former world champion Anthony Crolla is part of the informed cohort of observers who believe he could make waves.

‘One of the harder parts in it all was learning that I was about to be added to the England squad when I fell ill,’ he says. ‘You have to get over that and wow, I feel like I have a chance to show what I can do.
